BERT4Rec explicitly recognizes the mismatch between random masked-item reconstruction and future-item ranking: inference appends MASK, and training includes examples masking only the final item. This supports testing terminal masking within the existing single model, without exposing targets through bidirectional inputs. Loss accounting matters: the original objective averages masked-target losses within each sequence; pooling all masked tokens instead changes sequence weighting. See [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690).

Gradient direction, magnitude and sampling variance require separate measurements. [PCGrad](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782) addresses conflicting gradient directions; [GradNorm](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/chen18a.html) addresses gradient-scale imbalance. Neither establishes that allocation shares predict ranking quality. Recommended diagnostic inference: separately for embeddings and encoder, compute coefficient-weighted branch gradients using actual loss denominators; report norms, dot products, cosine conflict rates and covariance across repeated batches. Verify their sum reproduces the implemented total-loss gradient before interpreting conflicts.

First resolve provenance: fixed 64/64 branch allocation differs from independent Bernoulli allocation, even when expected counts match; conditioning on exact counts changes sampling variance. Bind diagnostics to checkpoint identity, sampler configuration, realized counts, masked-target counts, denominators and coefficients. [NVIDIA’s reproducible-checkpoint guidance](https://github.com/NVIDIA/framework-reproducibility/blob/master/doc/d9m/pytorch.md) additionally calls for model, optimizer, loader, step and RNG states. Proposed executable checks: reconstruct losses and gradients, then compare checkpoint-loaded predictor scores on identical appended-MASK inputs. Finally test whether measured conflicts predict terminal-target loss or validation ranking failures through controlled single-model ablations; geometry alone is insufficient evidence.
